prompt: Why are epoxides so much more reactive than typical ethers?

options.label: The 3-membered ring has ~27 kcal/mol of ring strain; relieving strain is a large driving force.
The C–O bond is more polar.
Resonance stabilization of the open form.
The oxygen has a formal + charge.

explanation: Epoxides have significant angle strain (60° vs ideal 109.5°) and torsional strain. Opening the ring releases that strain, making epoxides reactive even with weak nucleophiles — unlike normal ethers.
